clue.text: Return of American poet mostly creates excitement

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the abbreviation is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: US is the standard abbreviation for American

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the poet's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Edmund Spenser wrote The Faerie Queene

explanation.surface: A US poet's comeback tour gets the literary world buzzing.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspense is the anxious, eager uncertainty of waiting to see what happens, a kind of thrilled tension.

clue.text: Some tabloids principally have control over breaking news

indicators.note: principally means chiefly, pointing to the first letter of each word

parts.note: the first letters of Some and tabloids
to oppress is to keep others under harsh control

explanation.surface: A few tabloids essentially dominate the latest news.
explanation.definitionFit: Stop press was late news inserted into a newspaper after printing began, the old equivalent of breaking news.

clue.text: Cover in outbuilding not quite retaining warmth

indicators.note: to retain is to hold in, so one piece is kept inside the other
not quite all means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a shed is an outbuilding
heat is warmth

explanation.surface: Taking shelter in an outhouse that barely keeps the heat in.
explanation.definitionFit: To sheathe is to put into a sheath or encase, so to cover.

clue.text: Apprentice missing first money-making initiative

indicators.note: missing the first means its opening letter is dropped

parts.note: a learner is an apprentice

explanation.surface: A trainee misses out on the first business scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: An earner is a source of income, as in a nice little earner, a scheme that brings in money.

clue.text: Small sheep that is dozier than all the others?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a tup is a ram
id est is Latin for that is, abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: A little sheep that is the dimmest of the flock.
explanation.walkthrough: TUP is a British dialect word for a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: Stupidest is the superlative of stupid, so dozier, that is dimmer, than every other one.

clue.text: Having come out, feel ultimately enthralled by a period of growth

indicators.note: to be enthralled by something is to be held captive inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: A plus BOOM, an economic period of growth

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end, so only the last letter of feel is kept

parts.note: the last letter of feel

explanation.surface: Someone who has just come out feels caught up in a time of personal growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having come out' sounds like a personal revelation, but it means flowers that have opened.
explanation.definitionFit: Flowers that are abloom are in blossom, that is, their buds have come out.

clue.text: Loyal friend starts to act tearful, consumed by feelings of tenderness

indicators.note: consumed by means swallowed inside

parts.note: aches are feelings of soreness, tenderness in the body

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters

parts.note: the first letters of act and tearful

explanation.surface: A faithful companion is moved to tears by affectionate emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tenderness' suggests affection, but it means physical soreness.
explanation.definitionFit: Achates is the faithful companion of Aeneas in Virgil's Aeneid, his name a byword for a loyal friend.

clue.text: Plant secures agreements from French state

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast inside

parts.note: a liana is a tropical climbing plant
oui is French for yes

explanation.surface: A factory obtains contracts from the French government.
explanation.walkthrough: Plant suggests a factory, and 'French state' reads as one phrase; the state is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Louisiana is a US state, named after the French king Louis XIV.

clue.text: Give a speech about training for work

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to orate is to give a speech
PE is physical education

explanation.surface: Deliver a talk about job training.
explanation.definitionFit: To operate is to function or run, as a machine works.

clue.text: Source of e.g. iron and gold close to Kalgoorlie

parts.note: or is the heraldic term for gold

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the town's final letter is used

parts.note: the last letter of Kalgoorlie

explanation.surface: Iron and gold are mined near Kalgoorlie, the Western Australian gold-rush town.
explanation.walkthrough: Kalgoorlie is a famous mining town in Western Australia, which makes 'close to Kalgoorlie' read like a location.
explanation.definitionFit: Ore is the rock mined and smelted to extract metals such as iron.

clue.text: Hooligan put up a fight

parts.note: a rough is a violent, rowdy person
to house someone is to put them up

explanation.surface: A thug resisted arrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up a fight' reads as one phrase; it splits so that 'fight' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A roughhouse is a rowdy brawl or scuffle, and as a verb it means to fight boisterously.

clue.text: Sad way to refer to retiring

parts.note: a path is a way

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the word for refer to runs backwards

parts.note: to cite is to refer to

explanation.surface: A rather unkind way to describe someone shy and retiring.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathetic means pitiful or woeful, so sad in the sense of feeble or deplorable.

clue.text: Diagnostic test introduced by group of workers from Italy

parts.note: TU stands for trade union
a scan is a medical diagnostic test

explanation.surface: A medical test brought in by a trade union from Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Introduced by' means the union's letters come first.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuscan describes Tuscany, a region of central Italy, so a Tuscan thing comes from Italy.

clue.text: Former City CEO, perhaps

parts.note: ex means former
EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: A one-time chief executive in the City of London.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, whose postcodes begin EC.
explanation.definitionFit: An exec is an executive, and a chief executive officer is one example.

clue.text: Showing restraint in blocking pictures on a website, say

indicators.note: something blocking a channel sits in the middle of it

parts.note: content is the material, such as pictures, on a website
taken as written

explanation.surface: A site moderator shows self-control by blocking images.
explanation.definitionFit: Continent means self-restrained, especially in sexual matters or bodily functions.

clue.text: Surrounded by low-pitched backing, a harp's played like a lute?

indicators.note: backing means moving in reverse, so the word for low-pitched runs right to left
something surrounded by another thing sits inside it

parts.note: a deep note is low-pitched

indicators.note: played suggests the letters are handled freely and rearranged

parts.note: letters taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A harp played with a deep bass accompaniment sounds rather like a lute.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged harp letters sit inside the reversed bass word. The surface makes 'like a lute' sound like a sound; it describes the instrument's body.
explanation.definitionFit: A lute has a rounded body that is broad at the base and narrows towards the neck, the outline of a pear.

clue.text: Legal guideline in sport failing to protect group of stars

indicators.note: to protect something is to shield it by surrounding it

parts.note: RU is rugby union
a flaw is a failing
Leo is a constellation

explanation.surface: A sports regulation fails to look after its celebrity players.
explanation.walkthrough: The constellation goes between the two pieces of 'sport failing'.
explanation.definitionFit: The rule of law is the principle that everyone is subject to the law, a guiding legal principle.

clue.text: Negative mindset fades out with time

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Pessimism wears off as time passes.
explanation.definitionFit: Defeatism is the pessimistic expectation of failure, a negative outlook.

clue.text: Jam in second drawer on counter

parts.note: a stand is a stall or counter for selling
s is the abbreviation for second
a till is a cash drawer

explanation.surface: Something is stuck in the second drawer of a shop counter.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' places one piece after another, so second and drawer follow counter.
explanation.definitionFit: A traffic jam brings everything to a standstill, a complete halt.

clue.text: Yorkshire person's specific justification for being disloyal?

parts.note: in Yorkshire dialect the definite article is shortened to t'
a reason is a justification

explanation.surface: A Yorkshireman explains exactly why he betrayed someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Specific' stands for the definite article, which in Yorkshire speech is t', so 'the reason' becomes t'reason.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is the crime of betraying one's country, the gravest form of disloyalty.

clue.text: Mark is caught with grass in school

indicators.note: in places these pieces inside the school abbreviation

parts.note: sch is an abbreviation for school
c is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
to grass or rat is to inform on someone

explanation.surface: A pupil gets a mark for being caught with cannabis at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like the drug or the lawn; it is the slang verb for informing.
explanation.definitionFit: A scratch is a mark left on a surface, such as a scrape on paintwork.

clue.text: Occasional bits of false info in your dreams

indicators.note: occasional bits are taken now and then, here every other letter

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: Fragments of untrue information turn up in your dreams.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are scornful retorts meaning that something will never happen, an idiomatic expression of disbelief.

clue.text: Top expert on board?

parts.note: to surf is to ride a wave on a board
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: Who is the best member of the board of directors?
explanation.walkthrough: The board is a surfboard, not a boardroom: an expert on a board is a surf ace.
explanation.definitionFit: The surface is the top layer or outside of something.

clue.text: Crew has time for a drink

parts.note: a posse is a gang or crew
t is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: The team has time for a quick drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A posset is an old hot drink of milk curdled with ale or wine.

clue.text: High-ranking head of Inquisition appearing in Man of La Mancha?

indicators.note: to appear in something is to be inside it

parts.note: señor is Spanish for man, and La Mancha is in Spain

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of Inquisition

explanation.surface: A top Inquisitor turns up in the musical Man of La Mancha.
explanation.walkthrough: Man of La Mancha is a musical about Don Quixote; here it just means any Spanish man.
explanation.definitionFit: Senior means higher in rank or status, so a senior officer is high-ranking.

clue.text: Oregano sprinkled over the middle of meals? It's best avoided!

indicators.note: sprinkled herbs are scattered about, so these letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letter

parts.note: the central letter of meals

explanation.surface: Oregano scattered over a meal: a seasoning some diners would rather avoid.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-go area is a place people keep away from because it is dangerous or forbidden.

clue.text: Bins accept less rubbish

indicators.note: rubbish means poor or broken, so the letters before it are mangled into a new order

parts.note: letters taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Waste bins take in less rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bins' and 'rubbish' make a tidy refuse picture, but bins is British slang for glasses (from binoculars).
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, bins are eyeglasses, a pair of spectacles.

clue.text: Old fighter somewhat exhilaratingly knocked back

indicators.note: knocked back means sent backwards, so the found letters are read in reverse
somewhat means a part of, so the letters are found within the next word

parts.note: letters three to five of exhilaratingly

explanation.surface: A veteran boxer was thrillingly floored.
explanation.definitionFit: Muhammad Ali, the great heavyweight boxer, was a fighter of an earlier era.

clue.text: In the end, lovers naturally part

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, so only that is taken

parts.note: the last letter of lovers
natch is slang for naturally, of course

explanation.surface: Eventually, lovers inevitably split up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' looks like a verb for lovers separating; it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A snatch is a fragment or short piece, as in a snatch of song, so a part.

clue.text: Bit of power seized by joint US paramilitary force

indicators.note: something seized by another is held inside its grip

parts.note: a seam is a joint where two pieces meet
a watt is a unit of power

explanation.surface: Some electricity grabbed by a cannabis joint sounds like a raid waiting to happen.
explanation.definitionFit: A SWAT team is an American armed police unit for special weapons and tactics, a paramilitary squad.
